### Module 02 — Data Loading & Automated Profiling

# Data Loading & Automated Profiling

***
**Learning objectives**
- Load health data from CSV, Excel, and Parquet with production-grade options
- Generate an automated profiling report with `DataExplorer` and `skimr`
- Interpret profiling output sections: overview, variables, correlations, missing values
- Customise and export the report for sharing with clinical collaborators

**Estimated time:** 1 hour | **Level:** Beginner | **Libraries:** `dplyr` / tibble, `DataExplorer`, `skimr`, `readxl`, `arrow`

## 1. Setup & Dependency Check

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Install extras if needed (comment out after first run)
# install.packages(c("DataExplorer", "skimr", "visdat", "naniar", "arrow", "writexl", "readxl"))

library(tidyverse)
library(skimr)
library(DataExplorer)
library(visdat)
library(naniar)

mod02_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod02")
dir.create(mod02_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

if (requireNamespace("DataExplorer", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cat("DataExplorer imported successfully.\n")
} else {
  cat("Run: install.packages('DataExplorer')\n")
}

cat("dplyr version:", as.character(packageVersion("dplyr")), "\n")
```

## 2. Synthetic Hospital Discharge Dataset

```{r}
set.seed(42)
N <- 800

ages      <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
sexes     <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers    <- sample(c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
                    N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03))
drg_codes <- sample(c(470, 291, 392, 690, 871, 193, 247, 603), N, replace = TRUE)
drg_labels_map <- c(
  `470` = "Major joint replacement", `291` = "Heart failure & shock",
  `392` = "Esophagitis/misc GI",     `690` = "Kidney/UTI",
  `871` = "Septicemia",              `193` = "Simple pneumonia",
  `247` = "Perc cardiovasc w stent", `603` = "Cellulitis"
)
los_days   <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
charges    <- round(los_days * runif(N, 1800, 4200), 2)
charges[runif(N) < 0.08] <- NA_real_
primary_dx <- sample(c("E11.9", "I10", "N18.3", "I50.9", "J18.9", "A41.9", "M16.11", "N39.0"),
                     N, replace = TRUE)
admit_type <- sample(c("Emergency", "Elective", "Urgent", "Newborn"),
                     N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.52, 0.30, 0.16, 0.02))
set.seed(99)
df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = ages,
  sex           = sexes,
  payer         = payers,
  drg_code      = drg_codes,
  drg_label     = unname(drg_labels_map[as.character(drg_codes)]),
  primary_dx    = primary_dx,
  admit_type    = admit_type,
  los_days      = los_days,
  total_charge  = charges,
  diabetes      = rbinom(N, 1, 0.32),
  hypertension  = rbinom(N, 1, 0.45),
  ckd           = rbinom(N, 1, 0.15),
  heart_failure = rbinom(N, 1, 0.18),
  readmitted_30 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.14)
)
bins <- c(17, 44, 64, 74, 95)
df$age_group <- cut(df$age, breaks = bins, labels = c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+"))

start <- as.Date("2019-01-01")
set.seed(5)
n_days <- as.integer(as.Date("2023-12-31") - start)
df$admit_date     <- start + sample(0:(n_days - 1), N, replace = TRUE)
df$discharge_date <- df$admit_date + df$los_days
df <- df %>% arrange(admit_date)
cat(sprintf("Dataset: %d rows × %d columns\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))
head(df, 4)
```

## 3. Saving & Re-loading in Multiple Formats

```{r}
# CSV — most universal
readr::write_csv(df, file.path(mod02_dir, "discharges.csv"))

# Excel — useful for sharing with clinical stakeholders
writexl::write_xlsx(list(Discharges = df), file.path(mod02_dir, "discharges.xlsx"))

# Parquet — columnar, fast, preserves dtypes; preferred for large datasets
arrow::write_parquet(df, file.path(mod02_dir, "discharges.parquet"))

cat("Files written. Sizes:\n")
for (p in list.files(mod02_dir, full.names = TRUE)) {
  cat(sprintf("  %-30s  %.1f KB\n", basename(p), file.info(p)$size / 1024))
}
```

```{r}
# Re-load with production-grade options
df_csv <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(mod02_dir, "discharges.csv"),
  col_types = readr::cols(
    patient_id     = readr::col_character(),
    drg_code       = readr::col_integer(),
    admit_date     = readr::col_date(),
    discharge_date = readr::col_date()
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

df_parquet <- arrow::read_parquet(file.path(mod02_dir, "discharges.parquet"))

cat("CSV shape    :", nrow(df_csv), "x", ncol(df_csv), "\n")
cat("Parquet shape:", nrow(df_parquet), "x", ncol(df_parquet), "\n")
cat("\nParquet dtypes (preserved automatically):\n")
print(sapply(df_parquet, class))
```

## 4. Manual First-Pass Inspection

```{r}
# Always do this before profiling — catches obvious issues immediately
cat("=== Shape ===\n")
print(dim(df))

cat("\n=== dtypes ===\n")
print(sapply(df, class))

cat("\n=== Missing values ===\n")
miss <- colSums(is.na(df))
miss <- miss[miss > 0]
miss_tbl <- tibble(
  n_missing = miss,
  pct       = round(miss / nrow(df) * 100, 1)
)
print(miss_tbl)

cat("\n=== Numeric summary ===\n")
num_sum <- df %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    n    = ~ sum(!is.na(.x)),
    mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd   = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    p10  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
    p25  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    p50  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.50, na.rm = TRUE),
    p75  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    p90  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)
  ), .names = "{.col}__{.fn}")) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("variable", "stat"), names_sep = "__") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value)
print(num_sum %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1))))

cat("\n=== Categorical cardinality ===\n")
for (col in c("sex", "payer", "admit_type", "primary_dx", "drg_label")) {
  cat(sprintf("  %-15s: %3d unique\n", col, n_distinct(df[[col]])))
}
```

## 5. Automated Profiling with DataExplorer & skimr

```{r}
# Full profile — skimr (console) + DataExplorer (HTML report)
skim_result <- skim(df)
print(skim_result)

intro <- introduce(df)
cat("\nDataExplorer introduce() overview:\n")
print(intro)

vis_dat(df)
vis_miss(df)
naniar::gg_miss_var(df, show_pct = TRUE)
plot_intro(df)
plot_missing(df)
plot_correlation(df %>% select(where(is.numeric)), cor_args = list(use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))

cat("Profile computed.\n")
```

```{r}
# Save as self-contained HTML (share with collaborators — no R needed)
create_report(
  df,
  output_file  = "discharge_profile.html",
  output_dir   = mod02_dir,
  y            = NULL,
  report_title = "Hospital Discharge Dataset — Module 02 EDA",
  config       = configure_report(
    add_plot_prcomp       = FALSE,
    add_plot_boxplot      = TRUE,
    add_plot_correlation  = TRUE,
    add_introduce         = TRUE,
    add_plot_missing      = TRUE
  )
)
cat("Report saved to", file.path(mod02_dir, "discharge_profile.html"), "\n")
```

## 6. Interpreting the Profile Report

The report is divided into five sections. Here is what to look for in each.

| Section | What to check |
|---------|--------------|
| **Overview** | Number of variables, rows, missing cells, duplicate rows |
| **Variables** | Distribution shape, % missing, distinct count, warnings (high cardinality, skewed, zeros) |
| **Interactions** | Bivariate scatter plots — look for clusters or non-linear relationships |
| **Correlations** | Pearson (linear), Spearman (monotonic) — flag high correlations (>0.8) |
| **Missing values** | Bar chart + matrix — check if missingness clusters on specific patients or time periods |
| **Sample** | First/last rows — sanity check on values and date formatting |

```{r}
# --- Extract key stats programmatically from the profile object ---
intro <- introduce(df)

cat("=== Profile Overview ===\n")
cat(sprintf("  Dataset: %d rows, %d variables\n", intro$rows, intro$columns))
cat(sprintf("  Missing cells: %d (%.1f%%)\n",
            intro$total_missing_values, 100 * intro$total_missing_values / intro$total_observations))
cat(sprintf("  Duplicate rows: %d\n", sum(duplicated(df))))

cat("\n=== Variable-level warnings ===\n")
n <- nrow(df)
for (col in names(df)) {
  x <- df[[col]]
  n_miss <- sum(is.na(x))
  n_uniq <- n_distinct(x)
  alerts <- character(0)
  if (n_uniq == n) alerts <- c(alerts, "HIGH CARDINALITY")
  if (n_miss / n > 0.05) alerts <- c(alerts, "MISSING")
  if (is.numeric(x) && sum(x == 0, na.rm = TRUE) / n > 0.20) alerts <- c(alerts, "ZEROS")
  if (is.numeric(x) && sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
    sk <- mean((x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))^3, na.rm = TRUE) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)^3
    if (abs(sk) > 1) alerts <- c(alerts, "SKEWED")
  }
  if (length(alerts)) {
    for (a in alerts) cat(sprintf("  [%-20s] %s\n", a, col))
  }
}
```

## 7. Minimal Profile for Large Datasets

```{r}
# When dataset > 100k rows, use a skim-only / introduce-only profile for speed
intro_mini <- introduce(df)
skim_mini  <- skim(df)
print(intro_mini)

# A lighter HTML overview (plot_intro + plot_missing only)
html_mini <- file.path(mod02_dir, "discharge_profile_minimal.html")
# Write a compact summary table as a stand-in for DataExplorer minimal=TRUE
mini_tbl <- tibble(
  metric = c("rows", "columns", "missing_cells", "complete_rows", "numeric", "discrete"),
  value  = c(intro_mini$rows, intro_mini$columns, intro_mini$total_missing_values,
             intro_mini$complete_rows,
             intro_mini$continuous_columns, intro_mini$discrete_columns)
)
write_csv(mini_tbl, file.path(mod02_dir, "discharge_profile_minimal.csv"))
# Also emit a small HTML snippet
writeLines(
  c("<html><body><h1>Discharge Profile (minimal)</h1><pre>",
    paste(capture.output(print(intro_mini)), collapse = "\n"),
    "</pre></body></html>"),
  html_mini
)
cat("Minimal profile saved.\n")

# Compare report sizes
for (name in c("discharge_profile.html", "discharge_profile_minimal.html")) {
  fp <- file.path(mod02_dir, name)
  if (file.exists(fp)) {
    size_kb <- file.info(fp)$size / 1024
    cat(sprintf("  %-45s: %.0f KB\n", name, size_kb))
  }
}
```

## 8. Knowledge Check

1. Why is Parquet preferred over CSV for large health datasets?
2. In the profile report, what does a 'HIGH CARDINALITY' warning mean for `patient_id`?
3. `total_charge` has 8% missing values. What should you investigate before imputing?
4. The profile shows Pearson correlation of 0.82 between `los_days` and `total_charge`. Is this expected? Why?
5. Re-run the profile on only the Medicare subgroup. Do the warnings change?

```{r}
# --- Exercise 5 ---
df_medicare <- df %>% filter(payer == "Medicare")
cat("Medicare subgroup profile (skimr):\n")
print(skim(df_medicare))
print(introduce(df_medicare))
plot_intro(df_medicare)
plot_missing(df_medicare)
```
